text: Hello, and welcome to live coverage of this Premier League fixture, as Brighton host Newcastle at the Amex Stadium.
Brighton’s perfect start to the season came crashing down against West Ham last time out, losing 3-1 at home to the Hammers despite dominating large parts of the game.
However, with the arrival of Barcelona winger Ansu Fati showing a real statement of intent from the Seagulls, Roberto De Zerbi’s side will be confident they can return to winning ways here.
Newcastle’s 5-1 win over Aston Villa on the opening day feels like some time ago now, with the Magpies having lost both matches since to Manchester City and Liverpool respectively.

Eddie Howe’s men surrendered a 1-0 lead as Darwin Nunez’s late brace turned things around for 10-man Liverpool last time out, and the visitors will be anxious to avoid extending their losing run to three games.
De Zerbi makes three changes from the side beaten by West Ham at the Amex, with Danny Welbeck injured and Adam Webster and former Magpie James Milner dropping to the bench.
Jan-Paul van Hecke and Joel Veltman slot into the right side of defence, while Joao Pedro will play in behind Evan Ferguson up front for the Seagulls.
Ansu Fati only signed from Barcelona yesterday, meaning this game comes a fraction too soon for the Spanish wonderkid.
A key injury at the back has forced Eddie Howe into some defensive changes, with the absent Sven Botman being replaced by Matt Targett.

Dan Burn moves centrally to accommodate the left-back, while further forward, Joelinton starts alongside Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes in midfield, the Brazilian keeping his place despite also picking up a knock last time out.
The two teams head onto the pitch at a sun-kissed Amex Stadium, and we're just minutes away from kick-off between two sides who are both playing European football this season!
Ferguson gets the game underway for Brighton, and we're off and running on the south coast!
CHANCE!!! A massive early opening for Newcastle! Dunk slips on the edge of his own box, allowing Guimaraes' forward ball to travel into Isak's path.
The Swede bursts into the area, but Van Hecke gets across brilliantly and the eventual Isak shot ricochets behind for a goal-kick!
WIDE!! Tonali cuts out an Estupinan clearance and pulls the ball back from the byline.
Isak is again the target and snatches at a shot, but drills his strike into the ground and behind!
OVER!!! Gross cuts inside to find March, who does likewise before shooting from the edge of the box.
His fizzer of an effort has Pope at full stretch, but the goalkeeper is nowhere near it as the ball whistles over the top!
Veltman plays March in behind Targett, but the winger's low cross hits the sliding Newcastle left-back and goes behind for a corner!
Pedro climbs high from the Brighton corner, but his glancing header doesn't trouble Pope and sails wide of the far post.

Newcastle's last away win against Brighton came in February 2017 in the Championship, with the Magpies failing to win any of their six visits in the Premier League since the pair were promoted at the end of that 2016-17 campaign.
SAVED!!! March darts around the outside of Targett and floats a cross for the near post.
It's an awkward one for Pope to deal with, and the goalkeeper unconvincingly paws the ball behind for a Brighton corner!
Dunk's cushioned header at the far post nods the ball back towards Estupinan, but the Ecuadorian's first-time shot from the edge of the box bounces wide for a goal-kick!

Brighton haven’t lost consecutive games since October 2022, which came in De Zerbi’s second and third games in charge, and will be hoping to avoid equalling that record following their 3-1 home loss to West Ham last time out.
SAVED!!! A lovely first-time ball from Gilmour slips Ferguson in behind the defence.
He holds off Schar to shoot low from the left side of the box, but he doesn't do enough to trouble Pope, who collects with ease!
SAVED!!! Almiron collects a wide pass and charges into the area.
He takes on Dunk and puts in a cross, which takes a wicked deflection off the Brighton captain and forces Verbruggen into action, saving at his near post to prevent an own-goal!
Newcastle's corner is an easy one for Brighton to deal with, and the Seagulls are soon flying forward on the break.
Mitoma leads them, but his effort from the edge of the box is blocked and Pope collects for the visitors.
Newcastle launch a counter-attack of their own after Pedro is dispossessed in their box.
Isak races onto the ball and breezes past Dunk into the box, but Gordon overruns the striker's cross and the chance comes to nothing!
A Brighton corner is headed back across the face of goal by Dunk, but neither Mitoma nor March can get a decent opening to shoot and Newcastle eventually clear their lines!
Newcastle have lost their last two Premier League games, after losing just two of the previous 15 beforehand.
The Magpies last suffered three consecutive league defeats in March and April 2022.
Gordon flies in late and loses a 50-50 challenge with Van Hecke, and the showing of the studs warrants the game's first yellow card for the Newcastle winger.

Since the start of last season, Newcastle’s seven Premier League defeats have come against teams who started the day, on average, in sixth position, with Brighton coming into this game sixth in the table.
Indeed, 69 per cent of Eddie Howe’s Premier League defeats with the Magpies have come against sides starting the day in the top six (11 of 16).
Schar fires a long ball forward with Joelinton the target, but he can't bring it down to shoot before Verbruggen collects for Brighton.
GOOOOOAAAAALLL!!!! Brighton lead at the Amex!! It's a horror show for Pope, whose rushed, intercepted clearance leaves Newcastle stretched at the back.

He saves Mitoma's close-range effort after the winger is played in, but makes an absolute meal of Gilmour's long-range follow-up, spilling the ball right into Ferguson's path for the striker to tap home! 1-0 to the hosts in slightly fortunate circumstances, but after braving an early storm from Newcastle there's no doubting Brighton have been the better side so far!
WIDE!!! Almost an immediate response from Newcastle.
Gordon cuts inside from the left and engages defenders aplenty before finding Joelinton.
He skips into the box and fires a shot low, sending the ball rolling a yard wide of the post!
OVER!!! It's end-to-end alright!! Ferguson charges through the middle before finding Mitoma and Pedro ahead of him.
The latter is teed up in the centre and has the goal at his mercy, but can only fire over the top of the crossbar!

That Ferguson opener makes it 11 home games on the bounce in which Brighton have found the net, and the Seagulls are unbeaten in their last six when scoring first, dating back to an April loss against Nottingham Forest.
Isak spreads play wide to an advancing Tonali, who fires a low cross into the centre.
Gordon stretches for it, but can't quite reach the ball as it flashes across the face of goal!
With eight goals and two assists, Ferguson is only the second non-English player to reach 10 Premier League goal involvements while aged 18 or younger, after Cesc Fabregas (five goals, 10 assists).
The first half has absolutely flown by so far, with near-constant chances at each end.
Ferguson's breakthrough may have involved a stroke of fortune gift-wrapped to the teenager by Pope, but given what we've seen, that could be far from the last time the net bulges in this game.
Guimaraes appears to have shooting space on the edge of the box, but chooses instead to play in Tonali.
He gets into a tangle and loses possession in the area, but the ball drops to Isak, who fires a first-time shot into Van Hecke's outstretched leg!
Before this game, Brighton had the most shots (68), shots on target (30), touches in the opposition box (159) and accumulated the most xG (7.7) in the Premier League so far this season.
It’s the most shots on target a team has had in their opening three games in a season since eventual champions Manchester City's 31 in 2011-12!
Pedro gets the slightest of touches to Dunk's forward pass before being clattered off the ball by Schar.
It's late, ugly, and worthy of a yellow card, as the Newcastle centre-back goes into the book.
After Gordon heads behind for a corner, Gross hangs the delivery into the centre of the box.
Dunk rises and heads for goal, but can't direct his effort on target as the ball sails wide.
We'll play two additional minutes at the Amex, closing out a high-octane first half between these two evenly matched sides.
HALF-TIME: BRIGHTON AND HOVE ALBION 1-0 NEWCASTLE UNITED.

The hosts lead 1-0 at the break, with Ferguson profiting from a rare Pope error to give Brighton the lead in an otherwise even game! Newcastle started on the front foot, with Isak squandering two early chances before Verbruggen intervened to prevent a Dunk own-goal.
Brighton were just as dangerous going forward though, with March and Ferguson both forcing Pope into saves.
He did well with those, but spilled Gilmour's long-range strike straight to Ferguson.
The second half is shaping up to be a cracker, with either side more than capable of taking all three points here!
Pedro's forming a fine combination with Ferguson in Brighton's attack, registering two first-half shots and also creating two big chances.

He's won all six of his duels so far, including a dribble and two aerial contests apiece, while Ferguson has won three of his four and had two shots on target, one of which was the opener of course, to compile an xG of 0.82.
Isak kicks off for Newcastle, and we're back underway at the Amex!
Newcastle pile numbers into the box and spread play wide for Trippier to cross back in, but Mitoma cuts the ball out before being fouled by the full-back.
Brighton are unbeaten in their last 24 Premier League matches when leading at half-time, stretching over more than two seasons and dating back to May 2021 against Wolves.
March charges down the right and dinks a reverse pass into Ferguson's path, but he can't get to the ball before Pope and the goalkeeper cleans up for Newcastle.
CHANCE!!! March picks Targett's pocket and races in behind the Newcastle left-back.
His cross from the byline sits up for Pedro, but he can't get a shot away before the ball is knocked clear by the visitors!

CHANCE!! Sloppy play at the back almost costs Newcastle dearly! Gross' cross inside for Pedro is dealt with, but a poor pass out of defence from Trippier gives the Brazilian another chance which, luckily for the Magpies, he's unable to take!
Gross whips a looping cross towards the back post at a Brighton corner, where Ferguson climbs high but can't send the ball towards the intended target!
Eddie Howe makes a triple change, looking to put a stop to the seemingly endless stream of Brighton attacks, with the first seeing Callum Wilson replace Joelinton for the Magpies.
Almiron also comes off, and Elliot Anderson will replace the Paraguayan as Newcastle make alterations to their attack.
The last change is more like-for-like, as Sean Longstaff comes on for Tonali in Newcastle's midfield.
Forward come Newcastle as Isak beats Veltman down the left side, before seeing his cross blocked behind for a corner off Van Hecke.
Trippier whips in a dangerous corner for Newcastle, leaving Verbruggen scrambling in the Brighton goalmouth as it curls around the far post!
Longstaff's throughball sends Isak running into space down the left and into the box, but Van Hecke stands his ground well to put the ball behind for another Newcastle corner.
Newcastle are yet to have a shot on target in the match and haven't had a single shot since the 39th minute - worrying signs for Eddie Howe's men.

GOOOOOOOAAAAAAALLLL!!!! What a finish from Ferguson!!! Gilmour squeezes a pass forward to the Irishman, who turns and lets fly from 25 yards, finding the bottom-right corner with a composed, curling strike! Pope wasn't far away but couldn't get down quick enough, and this electrifying teenager nets his second of the game to put Brighton 2-0 up and in complete command!
Gilmour did well to make that pass, being both off-balance and under pressure from Anderson, but managed to open up a pocket of space for Ferguson to exploit - and the striker did just that!
BLOCKED!!! Newcastle launch an attack in response as Isak and Targett combine down the left.
The latter's low cross rolls all the way through to Gordon, whose first-time shot is blazed wide!
Isak concedes a free-kick for a foul on Veltman, which Brighton want to take quickly but are prevented from doing so by Targett.
That's time-wasting straight out of the textbook, and as such the Newcastle defender is shown a yellow card.

GOOOOOAAAAALLL!!!! The teenager gets three!!! Mitoma glides his way to the edge of the box before finding Ferguson, and the 18-year-old's early left-footed shot takes a massive deflection off Schar, wrong-footing Pope who can only watch as the ball nestles in the bottom corner! The goal is Ferguson's though as the initial shot was on target, and he completes his hat-trick to put Brighton 3-0 up!

Mitoma's mere presence in the final third drew Newcastle's defenders towards him, and opened up space for Ferguson to get that shot away early, catching the back four off-guard as Brighton all-but seal the points here.
Ferguson is only the fourth player to score a Premier League hat-trick aged 18 or younger, after Chris Bart-Williams, Robbie Fowler, and Michael Owen (who did so four times).
Isak's been Newcastle's only real outlet in attack, but comes off now for Harvey Barnes to see out the latter stages of what's turning out to be a nightmare for the Magpies.
Targett has been run ragged at times by Brighton's constant wide attacking, and Jamaal Lascelles' introduction in his place is clearly an attempt to shore up the Newcastle defence.
Barnes cuts inside and looks to find the far corner with a curling effort, but Van Hecke dives across to nod the ball away from danger!
Burn knows full well March has him beaten all ends up for pace, and takes down the winger off the ball to prevent a breakaway before shortly being shown a yellow card.
He knew that one was coming.
Brighton finally make their first changes of a game they've ended up coasting in, as the influential Gilmour comes off for Mahmoud Dahoud.
Pedro has also stood out amid a top-class Brighton team performance, and Tariq Lamptey replaces the forward late on with the game almost won.

Estupinan, Ferguson and Trippier all end up on the deck following an almighty collision, but the three are soon back on their feet and ready to play out the last 10 minutes of what has become a fairly one-sided contest on the south coast.
March has been his lively, dangerous, consistent self throughout this game, and comes off following another superb performance for Adam Lallana to see out proceedings.
Hat-trick hero Ferguson is withdrawn to thunderous applause by the Amex faithful, and James Milner, who signed for Newcastle a few months before Ferguson was even born in 2004, will replace him.
Lamptey leaves Burn for dead as he surges into the final third for Brighton.
His cross comes to nothing and Guimaraes recovers it for the visitors, but he's soon caught late by the Seagulls substitute and Lamptey goes into the book.
With five minutes to go, Newcastle are still yet to register a shot on target so far in this game.
After their electric start with two chances in the opening minutes, they've been woefully under-par since.
Gordon is taken down by Milner as he looks to cut inside from the right flank, and the veteran midfielder is the latest player to be shown a yellow card.
SAVED!!! Trippier's free-kick from the right is met by Schar at the back post, but his looping header is seen all the way and caught on the line by Verbruggen!

Gross trudges off having run the show yet again for the Seagulls, and having been replaced for the final throws by Simon Adingra, the 32-year-old playmaker can now look forward to his maiden international call-up for Germany.
He's earned it.
BLOCKED!! Milner sends Estupinan charging into open pasture down the left-hand side, and the flying Ecuadorian links up with Mitoma.
He stands up more defenders before teeing up Adingra, but the substitute's close-range shot is blocked and cleared away!
We're into SEVEN additional minutes at the Amex, which given how things have gone over the course of this game, should ease by for Brighton as they close in on three important points.

GOOOAAALLL!!! Likely just a consolation, but a very, very good one at that!!! Wilson latches onto a long pass forward from Longstaff, before flicking the ball around Van Hecke and stabbing it past Verbruggen into the back of the net!! A superb goal from the substitute to make it 3-1, and with five minutes of injury time to go, have the Magpies finally awoken to mount a late comeback here?
Newcastle haven't tried that type of pass enough in this game, with Longstaff stretching the defence and allowing Wilson the time and space he needed to fire home.
Newcastle have now scored three times in the last 15 minutes of their second halves this season, the most in the Premier League.
Dahoud wins a free-kick but certainly isn't happy with Lascelles, to the point that the referee shows him a yellow card for whatever was said by the German.
Mitoma looks to cut inside having received a forward pass from Milner, but strayed a yard offside and is flagged accordingly.

WIDE!!! A glorious chance to make it four!! Lamptey seizes onto a loose Newcastle pass at pace, and fires the ball across the face of goal to an arriving Mitoma, who can't turn it in at the back post with the goal at his mercy!
Guimaraes is shunted to the floor by Lallana as he tries to open a gap in midfield, and the flurry of late yellow cards continues with the Brighton midfielder shown the latest one.
FULL-TIME: BRIGHTON AND HOVE ALBION 3-1 NEWCASTLE UNITED.

It's all over at the Amex, as Brighton return to the winner's circle with an emphatic performance! Evan Ferguson's hat-trick sees the teenager join an elite club of young Premier League stars, and seals three points for the dominant Seagulls.
Brighton dominated proceedings in the second half, and doubled their advantage when Ferguson curled home a beautiful strike from long range.
As with his first, there was an element of luck about his third too, with his shot deflecting off Schar into the net as Newcastle faltered at the back.

Wilson's impressive stoppage-time finish restored some parity for the visitors, but on the whole, Newcastle were well beaten in a 3-1 defeat and lose for the third game running, while Brighton continue an impressive start to the season with their third win in four matches.
That win puts paid to any thought of Brighton having a soft underbelly, with the Seagulls soaring back into the top four on nine points.
It's a far bleaker situation for Newcastle though, who drop further to 13th in the table, their +4 goal difference from that opening day eradicated by three straight defeats.
It's still early in the campaign, but Eddie Howe has a task on his hands to turn around a squad who lost just five times in 38 league games last season.
That's all from us, we hope you enjoyed the game! As always, we'll see you for the next one - goodbye!
